 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Arizona's RJ Godfrey is the latest former college athlete to suddenly regain his eligibility thanks to a last-second decision by a judge. Godfrey was reportedly granted a preliminary injunction Tuesday, according to Field of 68.
 Because of that, Godfrey is eligible to play for Arizona. The ruling comes a day before No. 12 Arizona is set to take on No. 3 UConn.
 While Godfrey is eligible to play Wednesday, it's unclear whether he'll make an appearance in the contest. It's possible the senior will need more time to get ready after missing the start of the season due to a dispute over his eligibility.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With the news, Godfrey joins TCU's Robbie Avila as two of the bigger names to earn college eligibility in the middle of the season. Avila was granted a preliminary injunction to return to college in early November. He initially wanted to return to St. Louis, but the team did not have a roster spot for him. Because of that, Avila was able to join TCU . While he was technically eligible for the team's game against Milwaukee on Friday, Avila did not play. TCU's next game will take place Thursday against Texas A&M. It's unclear whether he'll appear in that contest.
 Godfrey was among the 16 former college basketball players who sued the NCAA for an additional year of college eligibility. That lawsuit, which was filed in Georgia, appeared to hit a snag in October after oral arguments were scheduled for January, deep into the college-basketball season. Godfrey and the other plaintiffs withdrew their names from the lawsuit following that development and explored other avenues in which they could continue their fight.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For Godfrey, that meant filing a lawsuit against the Arizona Board of Regents. That suit, which was filed Nov. 5, sought a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction that would give Godfrey a fifth year of college eligibility.
 That preliminary injunction was granted Tuesday.
 The fight over college eligibility has not been limited to just basketball. In September, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris earned a fifth-year of college football eligibility. Despite both players being available, LSU left them off the team's roster over threats from the SEC.
 The Big 12 has yet to make any public statements after both Avila and Godfrey were granted their preliminary injunctions. Barring any statements from the conference, Godfrey and Avila appear poised to make their season debuts.
